artboards.role: Single desktop screen for the pizzeria's public menu: header nav, hero, category filter row, 3x3 menu grid, a floating cart-summary bar, and footer. The linked node is already a single FRAME (not a CANVAS with multiple siblings), so there is exactly one artboard to review, not several.

excluded.reason: No OS/device chrome, browser mockup frame, status bar, notch, or home-indicator scaffolding was found anywhere in the tree — this is a plain desktop web frame (1440x2432) with no simulated device bezel, so nothing needed exclusion on that basis. Listed here explicitly per instructions, since the absence itself is a checked fact, not an omission.

open_questions.detail: The cart-summary node sits at y=2216, painted BEHIND the footer (footer starts at y=1956 and is a later, higher z sibling), so it is invisible in the rendered PNG at its literal Figma coordinates — confirmed by sampling that pixel region, which shows plain footer background, not the bar. A static-flow placement there would visually hide the bar behind the footer, which cannot be the intent of a 'cart summary' the shopper needs to see and act on.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement CartSummaryBar as a fixed-position bar pinned to the bottom of the viewport (visible over page content while scrolling), shown whenever the cart has at least one item, rather than as a bar living in the normal document flow at its literal Figma y-offset.

options.label: Fixed to viewport bottom while cart has items — matches typical checkout-bar UX and explains why Figma parked it off in unused canvas space
Static, in-flow element placed exactly where drawn (behind/above footer per stacking order) — reproduces the frame literally, but would be hidden from users in the current stacking order

open_questions.detail: Every category tag observed (Classic, Specialty, Vegetarian, Sides & Drinks) renders in the same green (#2A7043) in both the node fills and the PNG — there is no per-category color variation despite 4 distinct category names, and no red/other-hued tag appears anywhere in the grid to test a second mapping.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Treat the category tag as a single flat 'muted-success-green' style applied to all categories, not a category-to-color lookup table, since no evidence of variation exists in this frame.

open_questions.topic: Tiramisu della Casa filed under 'Sides & Drinks'
open_questions.detail: The dessert 'Tiramisu della Casa' (13:171) is tagged 'Sides & Drinks' rather than a dedicated 'Desserts' category. The filter row (13:27) only offers All/Classic/Specialty/Vegetarian/Sides & Drinks, so this is consistent with the available filters, just a possibly-loose content grouping.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Keep the content as authored (category = 'Sides & Drinks') since it is consistent with the filter set actually drawn; not treated as a build defect.

open_questions.detail: The frame only shows one active pill ('All') and four inactive pills at rest — no hover, focus-visible, or disabled visual is drawn for any pill, and no empty-state is drawn for a category with zero matching items.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement standard hover/focus affordances (e.g. subtle background tint on hover, visible focus ring) using the existing inactive/active token pair, and add a simple 'No items in this category' empty state, without inventing new colors beyond the tokens already distilled.

open_questions.detail: The rendered PNG shows '30 mins' in a green accent within the otherwise white 'Estimated delivery:' label, but the Figma text node (13:19) is a single TEXT node with one uniform white fill and no color-run/segment data distinguishing '30 mins' from the rest of the string.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Split the string in code into a static label plus a dynamic value span, and style the value span with the same green used for category tags (#2A7043), since that's the only green token in the palette and matches the PNG by eye.
